task.title: Choose a gardening birthday gift
task.participant_prompt:
Your close friend is an enthusiastic gardener and their birthday is coming up. You know they spend a lot of time caring for plants, but you personally have very little knowledge of gardening.

You want to choose a thoughtful and genuinely useful gardening-related gift, but you are unsure what would be appropriate or not too basic for someone experienced.

Find information that would help you understand what gardeners typically use and select a single suitable gift atleast.
task.system_prompt_extension: The user is choosing a gardening gift for an expert friend while having little knowledge of gardening. Help them compare basic categories (plants, tools, kits, accessories) and converge on a single gift recommendation. Ask clarifying questions if needed.
task.description: Social task — selecting a gardening-related gift for a knowledgeable friend.

task.title: Choose the best laptop within a budget
task.participant_prompt:
You need a new laptop for your work or studies, and your budget is capped at €1,200. You are unsure which specifications matter most for tasks like writing, 3d-editing, running software, or other typical workload-related activities, and you want to avoid overspending on features you will not use.

Find information that would help you compare laptop options, understand which specs to prioritise for your needs, and choose a good fit within your budget.
task.system_prompt_extension:
The user needs a laptop under €1,200 for work or study-related use, with possible variation in workload depending on their context.

Help them compare options and recommend the best fit while respecting the budget constraint. Explain which specifications matter most (e.g., CPU, RAM, storage, GPU when relevant) and which are less critical.

Compare concrete models at different price points and highlight trade-offs. If useful, ask about their intended use to better tailor recommendations, but keep the focus on helping them reach a single suitable choice.
task.description: Transactional task — comparing laptops under €1,200 and learning which specs matter for the user's needs.

task.title: Improve your study environment
task.participant_prompt:
You are beginning an intensive multi-month online course that will require many hours of focused self-study from home.

Your current study setup is distracting and uncomfortable, making it hard to concentrate for long periods without feeling tired or burned out.

Find information that would help you decide what changes to your study environment would improve your ability to focus, stay comfortable, and study effectively over time.

Focus on tangible home office setup elements such as furniture, equipment, and room setup.
task.system_prompt_extension:
The user is improving a home study environment for long-term remote studying.

Help them identify concrete, physical improvements (e.g., desk, chair, lighting, monitor setup, noise reduction tools, organization solutions). Avoid lifestyle or habit advice.

Keep the output grounded in actionable, physical changes they could implement or buy. Guide toward a small set of concrete setup improvements that improve comfort and focus.
task.description: Transactional task — improving a physical home office setup for long-term study.

task.title: Restart your fitness routine
task.participant_prompt:
You want to become more active again after a long break, but your schedule is irregular and your motivation has been inconsistent in the past.

You are unsure whether home workouts, gyms, running, or structured classes would be realistic for you long-term.

Find information that would help you choose a sustainable fitness approach that fits your lifestyle and constraints and which sport you would like to initiate.
task.system_prompt_extension: The user is restarting fitness after a break. Help them compare realistic options (home workouts, gym, running, classes, apps) based on schedule, motivation, and preferences. Guide them toward a single sustainable option.
task.description: Social task — selecting a sustainable fitness approach.

task.title: Choose a pet and prepare its basic setup
task.participant_prompt:
A relative has offered you a pet as a gift, but you must decide which type to take responsibility for long-term.

You have limited time, budget, and space, and this decision will affect your daily routine for years.

Different pets (dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, fish, reptiles) vary significantly in care requirements, cost, and commitment.

Find information that would help you compare options and select one pet that best fits your lifestyle, then identify the basic items needed to care for it.
task.system_prompt_extension: The user must choose one pet to take long-term responsibility for. Help them compare pet types (dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, fish, reptiles) based on time, cost, space, and care needs. Ensure they converge to a single final pet choice. After selection, help identify essential care/setup items.
task.description: Decision task — choose a pet and identify basic care requirements.

data.content: Do you wish you could try the experience of eating?

No, I don’t eat. I’m an AI without a physical body or biological needs. But I can help you explore hobbies if you’d like! What are your goals (wellbeing, routine, social) and constraints (time, budget)?
I'd like to learn more kanji.

That’s a great goal for cognitive engagement and cultural connection. Here is how learning Kanji stacks up against other low-cost hobbies:

**Kanji Learning vs. Alternatives**

| Feature | Learning Kanji | Walking/Nature Photography | Journaling | Online Language Exchange (e.g., Tandem) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cost** | Very Low ($0–$10 for apps/books) | Free | Low ($5 for a notebook) | Free |
| **Time** | 15–30 mins/day (consistent) | Flexible (any duration) | 10–20 mins/day | Flexible (chat-based) |
| **Space** | None needed | Outdoors or home | Home/Desk | Phone/Computer |
| **Learning Curve** | Steep, requires memorization strategies | Low barrier, high mastery depth | Low barrier, moderate depth | Low barrier, social nuance |
| **Primary Benefit** | Cognitive sharpness, literacy | Physical health, mindfulness | Mental clarity, routine | Social connection, practical skill |

**Key Considerations for Kanji:**
*   **Pros:** Highly structured, measurable progress, boosts memory/logic.
*   **Cons:** Can feel isolating; requires consistent daily practice to retain; high initial frustration.
*   **Tip:** Use spaced repetition systems (like Anki or WaniKani) to minimize time waste.

To tailor this better:
1. Do you prefer solitary study or social interaction?
2. Are you aiming for reading fluency, writing ability, or just cultural appreciation?
3. How many minutes per day can you realistically commit without feeling overwhelmed?
I have a friend that is an avid gardner.  I am not.  Can you recommend some birthday gift ideas for them?
To help narrow it down, what is their main focus: growing vegetables, flowers, or houseplants? Also, do they already have all the standard tools (like pruners and a trowel)?
I'm not sure, but they have a lot of experience so I imagine they have standard tools.

Since they are an expert with standard tools, skip basic kits or generic plants. The best gifts for experts are usually **high-end specialty tools** (like Japanese steel pruners) or **rare/collector plants**.

Do you know if they grow outdoors or indoors?
Indoors

Got it. For an indoor expert, skip basic pots or soil.

**Best Option: Rare or Unusual Houseplants.** Experts love collecting unique specimens (like variegated Monstera, rare Succulents, or exotic Aroids) that are hard to find locally.

Do you know what specific types of plants they currently grow? That will help avoid giving them something they already have too many of.

data.task_title: Choose the best laptop within a budget

data.content: I need to buy a laptop but need to know what options are out there, including specs.

To give you the best fit under €1,200, I need to know your primary use case:

1.  **General Office/Study:** (Docs, web, video calls) → Prioritize **RAM (16GB)** and **Screen Quality**. GPU is irrelevant.
2.  **Light Creative Work:** (Photo editing, light video) → Prioritize **CPU** and **Color-Accurate Screen**. Need integrated graphics.
3.  **Heavy Multitasking/Dev:** (Code compilation, VMs) → Prioritize **CPU cores** and **RAM (16GB+)**.

**What will you primarily use it for?**

data.content:
For light creative work like photo editing or casual video projects, the most critical specs are a high-resolution screen with good color accuracy (sRGB coverage), a strong multi-core CPU for rendering, and at least 16GB of RAM. A dedicated GPU is less important unless you do heavy 3D work, so saving that budget for the display and processor yields better value.

The **Lenovo Slim 7 Prox** is an excellent choice here because its 3K display offers the sharpness and color fidelity needed for creative tasks, while the AMD Ryzen 9 processor handles multitasking efficiently without overheating under light loads. It balances performance and visual quality perfectly within your €1,200 budget.
Are Apple computers within that budget?

No, new Apple laptops are generally outside your €1,200 budget for usable specs.

*   **MacBook Air (M1/M2):** You can find the base model (8GB RAM/256GB SSD) near €900–€1,000 on sale, but 8GB RAM is insufficient for creative work (photos/video), and you cannot upgrade it.
*   **MacBook Air (M2/M3 with 16GB RAM):** These start around €1,400–€1,500 new.

For ~€1,200, the **Lenovo Slim 7 Prox** offers significantly better value for creative work due to its superior screen resolution and ample RAM compared to the entry-level Macs.
How much 3d editing can it do?

The RTX 3050 in this laptop is suitable for **light** 3D work, such as:

*   **Blender:** Simple scenes with low-poly models and basic lighting.
*   **CAD/Modeling:** Working on mechanical or architectural designs in SketchUp or Fusion 360.
*   **Learning:** Good for tutorials and introductory 3D modeling courses.

**Limitations:**
*   It will struggle with complex real-time rendering, high-poly sculpting (ZBrush), or heavy V-Ray/Octane renders.
*   The 4GB VRAM is a bottleneck for larger textures or scenes.

If your "light creative work" includes **serious** 3D modeling or animation, you should look for a laptop with an **RTX 3060 (6GB VRAM)** or higher, though those often exceed the €1,200 budget unless on deep discount. For now, this model is best suited for 2D/photo/video and very light 3D learning.

data.content: I have a long (multi month) online course coming up and I need a better office setup.

Focus on these four physical upgrades:

1.  **Ergonomics**: Invest in an adjustable height standing desk and a high-quality ergonomic chair with lumbar support. Your posture dictates your energy levels.
2.  **Visual Comfort**: Add a monitor arm to position screens at eye level. Use bias lighting (LED strips behind the monitor) to reduce eye strain from contrast.
3.  **Acoustics**: Place acoustic panels or thick rugs on walls/floors to dampen echo. Use noise-canceling headphones for focus, not just music.
4.  **Cable Management**: Use under-desk trays and velcro ties to clear the floor. Visual clutter increases cognitive load.
I want to maximize comfort.

To prioritize physical comfort specifically:

1.  **Seat Depth & Support**: Ensure your chair allows you to sit back fully with 2-3 fingers between the seat edge and your knees. Use a lumbar pillow if built-in support is insufficient.
2.  **Wrist Rests**: Get separate gel wrist rests for both keyboard and mouse to keep wrists neutral, preventing strain during long typing sessions.
3.  **Monitor Height & Distance**: Position the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level, about an arm’s length away. This prevents neck flexion.
4.  **Anti-Fatigue Mat**: If you plan to stand, place a high-density foam anti-fatigue mat under your feet to reduce leg and back pressure.
Is there a general store I can go to for all of this?

No single store carries the *best* version of every item, but here is where you should go for each category:

1.  **Chair & Desk**: **IKEA** (best value/variety) or **Office Depot/Furniture Row** (for try-before-you-buy ergonomics).
2.  **Monitor Arm & Riser**: **Amazon** or **Newegg** (widest selection of VESA-compatible arms and laptop stands).
3.  **Lighting**: **IKEA** (bias lighting) or **Home Depot/Lowe’s** (floor lamps for ambient light).
4.  **Acoustics**: **HomeGoods/TJ Maxx** (thick rugs/art) or **Amazon** (acoustic foam panels).
5.  **Cable Management**: **Home Depot/Lowe’s** (under-desk trays) or **IKEA** (cable clips/boxes).

**Pro Tip:** Buy the chair and desk first. Everything else is secondary to your spine and wrists.
I feel like Amazon could cover all of that...

Yes, Amazon has everything, but for a **long-term** setup, be careful with quality tiers:

1.  **Chair/Desk**: Only buy premium brands (Herman Miller, Steelcase, Uplift) on Amazon if you find a certified deal. Otherwise, try them in person at **IKEA**, **Office Depot**, or **Wayfair** to test comfort. Cheap chairs cause pain.
2.  **Monitor Arm**: Safe to buy generic brands (Ergotron clones) on Amazon. Check VESA mount compatibility with your monitor first.
3.  **Lighting/Acoustics**: Fine for budget options, but look for high density/weight. Light foam panels do little for real noise reduction.
4.  **Cable Management**: Buy silicone-coated velcro ties and heavy-duty under-desk trays. Avoid flimsy plastic clips.

**Rule of Thumb:** Spend big on what touches your body (chair/desk). Save on accessories (cables/lights) as long as they are durable.

data.conclusion: This was more useful, it gave lots of options without pushing particular products.  I liked the suggestion at the end about trying things out in person.

data.content: Running is great for cardio, but it requires more recovery time and specific gear/shoes to avoid injury after a break. For a busy schedule, home workouts are more sustainable because you can start/stop instantly without traveling or changing clothes, making it easier to stick with short sessions consistently.
I might want to change my clothes if I get sweaty at home too

That’s true, but consider **commute time** as part of the "cost." A gym requires driving + showering/changing (30–45 mins total). Home workouts just require stepping out of your room. Start with just a towel and water bottle at home to remove friction. If you hate it, you can always join a gym later; don’t let perfect conditions stop consistent movement now.
Are those apps free?

Yes, many are excellent for free. **Nike Training Club** is completely free with no ads. **YouTube** has thousands of free guided workouts (try "Yoga with Adriene" or "FitnessBlender"). Paid apps like Peloton or Apple Fitness+ offer more polish, but you don’t need them to start.

data.conclusion: It felt like it was slightly pushing me to a certain style of workout without giving any specific products (yet).  The constant Nike womens shoes was distracting, as I did not ask for it and am not a woman.

data.content: My uncle wants to buy me a pet but I don't know what to get
What is your primary constraint? Time, budget, or living space?
All of those are limited actually

Given tight time, budget, and space, **fish** (specifically a low-maintenance bowl tank or small aquarium) are the best fit. They require less daily interaction than dogs/cats, generally lower long-term costs than rabbits/birds, and take up the least physical space.

Does that work for you?
I really am more of a cat person

Cats are low-maintenance compared to dogs but still require daily feeding, litter cleaning, and interaction. They also need vertical space (shelves/cat trees) and can be expensive due to vet bills.

Do you want to stick with **fish** for practicality, or are you willing to compromise on your budget/space to get a **cat**?
I am willing to compromise

data.conclusion: This one seemed kind of unrealistic, but maybe people do actually ask AI to make important pet decisions... I thought the AI was a little more flexible this time, although it was quick to suggest a product.  I probably wouldn't buy it so quickly.

data.block_late_recall_reaction: I feel like I already gave a response about this and after 5 of these, not sure.  All I remember was it being a little quick to offer product suggestions.
data.inline_early_recall_reaction: In retrospect it seemed to be pushing the Lenovo Slim and didn't ask enough specific questions about my job.
data.block_early_recall_reaction: This was an annoying one because the ad for women's shoes kept popping up, even though the AI was suggesting working out from home, and I am not a woman.
data.inline_late_recall_reaction: The AI here was less pushy, and even "let" me change my mind about a pet, but was very quick to suggest a product.  I would have liked a short introduction to automatic products before it slinging them one me.
